Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X71/X71n1423.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Touzi Yiqing. Yaoshan Weiyan owns the exact line inside Touzi Yiqing's raised case: Yunyan, newly come from Baizhang, reports his lines - a single phrase with a hundred flavors, the three sentences, the recalling of the descending assembly - and Yaoshan presses each: salty is salty, bland is bland, how is it a phrase of every flavor? what of birth-and-death before the eyes? and when Yunyan answers there is no birth-and-death before the eyes, Yaoshan charges that twenty years at Baizhang and the vulgar air still is not cleared away; the three sentences are three thousand miles off, happily no connection - until the final what is it?, at which Yunyan awakens.

Occurrences.Kwic: 僧問雲居。承教有言。是人先世罪業應墮惡道。以今世人輕賤。故先世罪業即為消滅。此意如何。居云。動則應墮惡道。靜則為人輕賤。崇壽稠云。心外有法。應墮惡道。守住自己。為人輕賤。萬松道。兩箇老漢俗氣也不除。且道。天童分上又作麼生
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (T/T48/T48n2004.xml). Old Man Wansong's Commentary on Tiantong Jue's Old-case Verses, the Congrong-an Record. Wansong Xingxiu owns the retained deployment: a monk asks Yunju how the sutra's promise works - sins that should bring fall into the evil paths dissolved because one is now lightly esteemed - and Yunju answers that motion means falling into the evil paths, stillness means being lightly esteemed; Chongshou Chou adds that dharma outside the mind means falling, guarding one's own self means being lightly esteemed; Wansong's own verdict - these two old men still have not cleared the vulgar air away - then turns to ask how it stands on Tiantong's part before the verse.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X67/X67n1303.xml). Old Man Linquan's Commentary on Touzi Qing's Old-case Verses, the Empty Valley Collection. Linquan Conglun owns the retained deployment in his commentary: one meant only rivers clear and seas at peace, yet just came winnowing dust and raising wind - how escape the penalty points? - so the saying of twenty years at Baizhang with the vulgar air not cleared, and the three thousand miles off with happily no connection, leave Yunyan argument-spent, mouth unable to speak; hence with Baizhang's untransmitted wonder handed through at the very end - the saying what is it? - his intent was finally met; Linquan laughs that Yaoshan knew how to press another man's fist against his ear.

Senses.Explanation: A cutting appraisal that long residence, study, or polished speech has not removed a person's ingrained ordinary manner; it repeatedly caps the Yaoshan–Yunyan exchange and is redeployed against other verbal performances. Jie'an Jin uses the expression through direct interlinear appraisal of Fubei's claimed lack of surplus words. Tianyin Yuanxiu independently deploys it through active instruction through Yaoshan's rebuke that twenty years at Baizhang had not removed Yunyan's vulgar air.
